practice_description.medium: Video, virtual worlds, immersive installation, multimedia, VR, photography, film
practice_description.practice_summary: Chinese multimedia artist who builds virtual worlds and cinematic environments exploring the collision of rapid urbanisation, digital culture, and lived reality in contemporary China. Her work maps the psychic geography of a society caught between communist legacy, hypercapitalist acceleration, and digital escapism.
practice_description.methodology: Cao Fei works at the intersection of documentary observation and speculative world-building. She embeds herself in specific social contexts -- factory floors (Whose Utopia), cosplay subcultures (COSPlayers), virtual communities (RMB City in Second Life), and Beijing's urban periphery (La Town) -- and constructs layered narratives that blend fiction, documentary, gaming aesthetics, and architectural modelling. Her later work uses VR and game engines to create persistent virtual environments. She collaborates with architects, programmers, and game developers. Represented by Vitamin Creative Space (Guangzhou) and Spruth Magers.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Cao Fei's practice of building persistent virtual worlds as artistic and social spaces directly models how art can function as substrate for collective inhabitation. Her work extends A(DAI)'s geographic range beyond Euro-American contexts and provides a critical non-Western perspective on digital commons and virtual urbanism.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes. RMB City was a persistent virtual world in Second Life that functioned as a platform others could inhabit, build within, and perform in. It was not a singular artwork but an environment -- a substrate for social, artistic, and economic activity. Her later VR works (Nova, Duotopia) similarly create inhabitable worlds.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Partially. RMB City was explicitly relational -- its form was shaped by the activities and constructions of its inhabitants over time. The world accumulated meaning through social interaction rather than singular authorial vision. Her documentary works also compose portraits from relational observations across communities.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Yes. RMB City evolved continuously from 2008 to 2011 as residents built, performed, and transacted within it. The virtual city changed shape based on inhabitant activity. Her game-engine works allow for variable pathways and non-linear exploration.

works.title: RMB City
works.description: A virtual city built in Second Life, combining iconic Chinese architectural forms (CCTV Tower, Oriental Pearl, factories) into a surreal digital metropolis. Functioned as a persistent online community where avatars could live, trade, and perform. Included RMB City Opera and RMB City: A Second Life City Planning.
works.relevance: Foundational example of art-as-virtual-infrastructure. A persistent world built as artwork that others inhabit and transform -- directly relevant to graph-curated generative environments where art is substrate rather than object.

works.title: Whose Utopia
works.description: Three-channel video filmed in an OSRAM light bulb factory in Guangzhou's Pearl River Delta, juxtaposing factory workers' assembly-line labour with their private fantasies -- dancing ballet, playing guitar -- staged on the factory floor.
works.relevance: Demonstrates Cao Fei's methodology of embedding in social systems and revealing hidden layers of desire and imagination within industrial infrastructure. Models how data from real systems (labour, production) can become artistic material.

works.title: Nova
works.description: Feature-length film and immersive installation (first shown at Serpentine Galleries) set in a virtual replica of a demolished Beijing neighbourhood. Uses motion capture, game engines, and CGI to create a ghostly digital archaeology of vanished urban space.
works.relevance: Shows how virtual world-building can preserve and recompose lost physical spaces. The work functions as a navigable environment rather than a linear narrative -- relevant to spatial, non-linear exhibition formats.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Cao Fei's virtual worlds function as proto-protocols -- systems with rules, economies, and social structures that shape behaviour. RMB City had its own virtual economy and social norms. However, her practice is more world-building than protocol-design in the strict infrastructure sense; she creates environments rather than governance systems.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: RMB City: a persistent virtual city with its own economic and social dynamics (2007-2011). The project included a virtual real estate system, performance programming, and community governance within Second Life's framework.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: RMB City was open to public inhabitation within Second Life -- anyone could visit and participate. However, Cao Fei's work overall operates within the commercial gallery system (Spruth Magers, major museum exhibitions). The virtual worlds were commons-like in their social function but not in their licensing or governance. Her work critiques enclosure (factory labour, urban demolition) without necessarily building alternative commons infrastructure.

governance_model.governance_detail: Cao Fei is the primary creative director of her projects, working with technical collaborators (programmers, architects, game developers) under her artistic direction. RMB City had a degree of participant self-governance within Second Life's platform, but Cao Fei determined the overall vision and framework. Her studio practice follows a solo artist model with project-specific collaborators.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Documentary subjects in works like Whose Utopia and COSPlayers are filmed with consent and often become active participants in staging their own narratives. RMB City inhabitants participated voluntarily in the open Second Life platform. No explicit consent frameworks beyond standard artistic practice.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo authorship with collaborative production. Cao Fei is credited as sole artist while working with technical teams. RMB City blurred authorship boundaries as inhabitants contributed to the world's form, but the project was authored and framed by Cao Fei.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: RMB City operated as a living virtual world from 2008 to 2011, evolving continuously before being deliberately shut down. Her video works are static once completed. Nova exists as both a fixed film and a navigable VR environment. Her practice oscillates between durational live systems (RMB City) and fixed cinematic works.

data_materiality.data_sources: Urban environments (Beijing, Pearl River Delta), factory production systems, Second Life virtual world data, motion capture performance data, architectural plans and demolished building documentation, Chinese internet culture and gaming aesthetics, cosplay communities.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Mixed. Documentary footage is self-generated through embedded observation. Second Life data was generated within a commercial platform. Motion capture data is produced by performers in studio. Architectural data for Nova was based on real demolished Beijing neighbourhoods. No scraped or non-consented data in the usual sense.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Cao Fei's work does not directly engage with ML embedding or latent spaces. However, her virtual worlds are navigable 3D spaces that function as spatial 'embeddings' of cultural meaning -- architectural forms encode political and social relationships. Her game-engine works create explorable possibility spaces.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes. Her work spans video, VR, architectural modelling, sound design, performance (motion capture), photography, and interactive installation.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Cao Fei's work occupies gallery spaces as immersive multi-channel video installations, VR environments, and architectural constructions. Nova at Serpentine transformed the gallery into a navigable virtual cityscape. RMB City existed entirely in virtual space (Second Life) but was exhibited through documentation, live feeds, and in-world events. Major solo exhibitions at MoMA PS1, Serpentine, Centre Pompidou, and UCCA Beijing.

interoperability.composability: Limited in terms of technical APIs or standard formats. RMB City existed within Second Life's platform (proprietary). Her VR and game-engine works are custom productions. However, the virtual worlds conceptually model composability -- they are environments designed to host other activities and creative acts.
interoperability.technical_openness: Closed system. Works are produced as discrete artistic projects within commercial gallery and museum frameworks. No open-source components or documented interfaces.

technical_approach.stack: Second Life (RMB City), Unreal Engine and Unity game engines, motion capture systems, CGI and VFX production, VR headset delivery, multi-channel video projection, architectural 3D modelling, cinema cameras and post-production

network_position.scene_affiliation: Chinese contemporary art (central figure), international biennial circuit (Venice Biennale 2003, 2007, 2015; Documenta [uncertain]), Serpentine Galleries (Nova 2019), MoMA PS1 (solo 2016), Centre Pompidou, UCCA Beijing, Guangzhou art scene (Vitamin Creative Space), virtual worlds and net art community (early Second Life art), commercial gallery circuit (Spruth Magers)
network_position.connections: Serpentine Galleries (Nova commission 2019), Vitamin Creative Space (long-term gallery), Spruth Magers (international representation), UCCA Beijing, Centre Pompidou, MoMA PS1. Bridges Chinese and international contemporary art worlds. Connected to digital art/virtual worlds discourse but primarily positioned in contemporary art mainstream.

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Cao Fei's practice provides crucial geographic and cultural diversity for A(DAI)'s graph -- extending beyond Euro-American digital art contexts into Chinese digital urbanism. Her virtual world-building methodology (RMB City) is a direct precedent for art-as-inhabitable-infrastructure. Her work could function as a reference node connecting digital commons, virtual urbanism, and non-Western perspectives on technology and society. As a conversation partner, she brings experience building persistent virtual worlds as artistic practice.
